second_witness: The archive copy was rendered in full (pp. 136-143) rather than grepped, and it is the reason this stint fired ZERO [sic:]. ⛔ MEASURED HERE: on this quire the archive copy is by far the worse witness. It manufactured NINE letter-, digit- and point-level readings that Gallica refutes -- 0263B seculo (Gallica sedulo), 0263B amplus (amplius), 0263C Ecce ergo (Ecce ego), 0263D invidita (invidia), 0268A labium , (labium.,), 0269D Omnes opus (Omne opus), 0271B Fecit et quinquaginta circulos (Facies et), 0272A VERS. 6 (VERS. 9), 0274B Marc. XLVI (Marc. XVI) -- and confirmed Gallica against our twin at only two sites (0262D annos, 0272C ad altera). Every one of the nine would have produced a false public claim against Migne if the archive had been the sole witness. This is the jbig2 symbol-substitution class of PL113-WITNESS-ENCODING.md, and its errors here are well-formed words that construe: 'Ecce ergo mittam angelum' reads perfectly and is not what Migne set.

reads.found: CHECKED ZERO at the foot of both columns, both layers. ⭐⭐ ONE RECOVERY: at 0263B the plate prints a HEBREW WORD our TEI drops -- 'quem Hebraei Chaldaico vocabulo thisri, תשרי Macedones ὑπερβεραῖον vocant'. Both copies show it; it is NOT among the six Hebrew words the pre-chunk recovery pass restored, so the Hebrew layer of this book is not complete. Consonants certain (ת-ש-ר-י, matching Migne's own transliteration 'thisri'); the plate appears to set at least one sub-letter point, which neither copy resolves at maximum available resolution, so the consonantal form is what is carried and the vocalisation is flagged open in the pending-patches file. FOUR ARCHIVE READINGS REFUTED BY GALLICA, all four leaving our twin correct: 'seculo curantes' (Gallica 'sedulo', which is also what construes), 'amplus tuba canunt' (Gallica 'amplius'), 'Ecce ergo mittam angelum' (Gallica 'Ecce ego', so NO [var:] against Ex 23:20 -- this one would have been a false public claim), 'invidita' (Gallica 'invidia'). CONFIRMED as printed: 'Solemnitatem vero mensis primitivorum' at 0263A, where the Vulgate has 'messis' (crux, no marker -- it is Migne's, in Rabanus's own prose, and it construes); 'unde justo, judicio Dei expulsi sunt' at 0264B, comma and all (Migne's own pointing, carried); 'Initium omnis peccati superbia' without 'est'; 'Alia littera: Benedicam panem et vinum tuum' and 'Alia littera. Emittam vespas ante te, et ejiciet Amorrhaeos' at 0264B-C -- Migne labels both divergences himself, so no marker is stacked on his own mark.
